raw_segments.text: And what is death, he asked, your mother's or yours are my own.
You saw only your mother die.
I see them pop off every day in the Mater and Richmond and
cut up into tribes in the dissecting room.
It's a beastly thing and nothing else.
You wouldn't kneel down to pray for your mother on her death bed when she asked you.
Because you have the cursed Jesuit strain in you,
only it's injected the wrong way.
To me, it's all a mockery and beastly.
Her cerebral lobes are not functioning.
She calls the doctor Sir Peter Teisel and picks buttercups off the quilt.
You crossed her last wish in death and yet you sulk with me because I don't
whinge like some hired mute from Laloet's.
I suppose I did say it.
I didn't mean to offend the memory of your mother.
